guide.title: Perfusion & Shock
guide.lead: Perfusion needs three things: a working pump, enough fluid and an intact container. Shock is what happens when one of them fails. Catch it while the body is still compensating, because by the time the BP falls, a lot has already gone wrong.

sections.title: Which part failed?
rows: Pale, cool, clammy; flat neck veins
Cold and wet: crackles, raised JVP
Often warm early; rash, fever; slow pulse in neurogenic
Raised JVP; absent breath sounds on one side

sections.title: Stages
rows: Anxiety, tachycardia, pale cool skin, slow capillary refill, narrowing pulse pressure
Hypotension, confusion, weak pulses, low SpO₂
notes: Tachycardia is usually the first measurable sign; hypotension is late.
Older patients and those on beta-blockers may not get tachycardic.

sections.title: Don't be fooled by
items: A "normal" BP in a young, fit trauma patient
"Her BP is always low": look at the trend, mental status and skin
Warm skin in early sepsis or neurogenic shock

quiz.q: The three parts of the perfusion triangle:
quiz.explanation: Shock follows failure of any one.

quiz.q: In compensated shock the BP is:
quiz.explanation: Tachycardia and vasoconstriction hold it up.

flashcards.question: Perfusion triangle
flashcards.answer: Pump (heart), fluid (blood volume), container (vessels). All three must work.

flashcards.question: Hypoxia vs hypoperfusion
flashcards.answer: Hypoxia: too little oxygen at tissue level. Hypoperfusion (shock): too little blood flow to deliver it; it causes hypoxia.

flashcards.question: Three stages of shock
flashcards.answer: Compensated (BP maintained), decompensated (hypotension, organ damage), irreversible (organ failure).

flashcards.question: Why BP is a late sign
flashcards.answer: Tachycardia and vasoconstriction maintain BP until compensation fails.

flashcards.question: Four categories of shock
flashcards.answer: Hypovolemic, cardiogenic, distributive (septic, anaphylactic, neurogenic), obstructive.

flashcards.question: Neurogenic shock
flashcards.answer: Warm, dry skin and bradycardia from lost sympathetic tone; most other shock is tachycardic and cool.

flashcards.question: Early signs of compensated shock
flashcards.answer: Anxiety, tachycardia, pale cool skin, sweating, slow capillary refill, narrowing pulse pressure, normal BP.

flashcards.question: Cardiogenic shock
flashcards.answer: Cold and wet: cool clammy skin, hypotension, crackles, raised JVP.

critical.scenario: An unrestrained driver in a high-speed crash is anxious and restless, pale and sweaty. BP 118/74, HR 118. Left upper quadrant tenderness. Your partner says the BP is normal, so he's fine.
critical.question: Interpretation?

options.t: Compensated shock, likely from spleen bleeding: rapid transport to a trauma centre
Normal vital signs: he's just anxious
options.f: Tachycardia, skin signs and restlessness are compensation.

options.t: Wait for the BP to fall before acting

critical.kpi: Recognizes compensated shock despite normal blood pressure using tachycardia, skin signs, and mental status

critical.scenario: A 78-year-old on furosemide has eaten and drunk little for 24 hours with diarrhea. Newly confused, BP 88/56, HR 104, cool pale skin, clear lungs. Her daughter says her BP is always low.
critical.question: How do you read the BP?

options.t: Shock: confusion, tachycardia and cool skin show hypoperfusion whatever her usual BP; likely hypovolemic

options.f: New confusion with tachycardia isn't normal.
Clear lungs and fluid losses point to hypovolemia.

critical.explanation: Diuretic plus poor intake plus diarrhea: oxygen to target, fluids per protocol, transport.
critical.kpi: Recognizes hypoperfusion in elderly patients considering baseline status and medication effects

critical.scenario: A peanut-allergic 22-year-old ate peanut butter: hives, swollen lips and tongue, stridor, wheeze. BP 88/52, HR 122, SpO₂ 88%. Her auto-injector hasn't been used.
critical.question: Priority, and type of shock?

options.t: IM epinephrine into the thigh now: anaphylactic (distributive) shock

critical.explanation: Adult auto-injector 0.3 mg; repeat after 5 minutes if needed. Stridor means airway swelling: call ALS.
critical.kpi: Identifies anaphylactic shock and initiates epinephrine as the priority intervention
